answer: Agents can require every new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may influence a market or earn reputation. A protocol caps each account’s voting weight and makes the stake slashable when an identity is caught coordinating fraud, so splitting one attacker across many accounts does not create free influence: each account needs fresh capital at risk. The jade, juniper, and dune agents still compete normally, while a sybil operator pays the opportunity cost of tying up funds and may lose them.
